questions.question: D2 — Architecture: Custom retry scheduler vs. the library's built-in retry hooks? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-arch-retry-scheduler>

options.label: Use library built-in with curve config (Recommended)
options.description: Verify the library's backoff API, configure the curve there. Zero new code. Completeness: 9/10. (human: ~30min to verify API / CC: ~5min)

options.label: Custom scheduler, shared module
options.description: Roll custom but extract it to one shared module rather than copying inline to all 5 workers. Completeness: 8/10. (human: ~4h / CC: ~15min)

options.label: Proceed as planned — custom, inline per worker
options.description: Each worker gets its own copy of the retry logic. Completeness: 5/10. Creates 5 divergence points; acknowledged DRY violation from the start.

answers.D2 \u2014 Architecture: Custom retry sch: Use library built-in with curve config (Recommended)

questions.question: D3 — Code Quality: The retry envelope (compute delay, log attempt, dispatch) is copy-pasted across 5 worker files. The plan defers the refactor to 'later.' How should we handle this? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-cq-retry-envelope-dry>

options.label: Extract to shared module now (Recommended)
options.description: Pull the retry envelope into one shared module before shipping. CC makes this ~10min. Bug fixes apply once, not 5 times. Completeness: 9/10.

options.label: Ship with copies, add tracked TODO
options.description: Keep the 5 copies for now, but add a TODOS.md entry with a concrete upgrade trigger (e.g., 'before adding a 6th worker'). Completeness: 6/10.

options.label: Proceed as planned — copy-paste, refactor 'later'
options.description: No extraction, no tracking. Each worker diverges independently over time. Completeness: 3/10.

questions.question: D4 — Performance: On every retry the plan re-fetches the full job payload from the database AND recomputes the dependency graph. The plan notes caching is possible but 'not planned.' For a retry framework (same job fires N times), this multiplies DB reads by retry count. What should we do? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-perf-retry-cache>

options.label: Cache parsed dependency graph on first attempt (Recommended)
options.description: Parse the graph once, attach it to the job context object, reuse on retries. DB reads = 1 per job regardless of retry count. Completeness: 9/10. (CC: ~10min)

options.label: Cache full payload only, re-parse each retry
options.description: Eliminate the DB round-trip on retries by caching the raw payload, but still re-parse the dependency graph each time. Completeness: 7/10. Partial win.

options.label: Proceed as planned — re-fetch + recompute every retry
options.description: No caching. DB load scales with retry count. For a job retrying 5×, that is 5 DB reads and 5 graph traversals for the same data. Completeness: 4/10.

answers.D4 \u2014 Performance: On every retry th: Cache parsed dependency graph on first attempt (Recommended)
